body: Anyone working on mapping the ASVS 4.0 with NIST 800-53 controls?

comments.body: This would likely be a 4.1 change, and it seems heavily requested, but it might create a new appendix or similar.

We have it done internally, within our organization, as mapping in an
Excel. Can we contribute?

On Tue, Jun 23, 2020 at 11:15 AM Andrew van der Stock <
notifications@github.com> wrote:

> This would likely be a 4.1 change, and it seems heavily requested, but it
> might create a new appendix or similar.
>

As a stopgap measure, I am willing to future-port [relevant material from v3.0.1 to 4.x](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/aba2f2ea68f79b713fcd333fdd17cb4a1086893b/3.0.1/NIST_800-53_Mapping_to_ASVS_301.html) given the item changes are not significant as a start.

Judging from the 4.x publication code for CSV and JSON, adjusting the relevant `Item`s for each `Requirement`s will suffice, am I not mistaken?
Does anyone have an updated sheet from ASVS 3.x to 4.x with NIST 800-53 controls? If I can be of any assistance for this task please let me know.

I'd be willing to collaborate on this too, but I am not sure who decides if the mapping is right or how to make this easily maintainable.

FYI to you and others interested, NIST recently [released the 800-53A Revision 5 final publication in September 2020](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/next-generation-security-and-privacy-controls-protecting-nations). I bumped this open issue when 800-53A Rev. 4 was published and the new updates were draft only. I am very interested in working with this group to consider the adoption of OSCAL (see #817) to further this work, for 800-53 controls but also to build off a new standard for security documentation, but checklists are a gray area as discussed with the OSCAL developers.

I will ping the ASVS devs on OWASP Slack to get more insight into how I can find a way to pitch in.

There are quite a few 800-53A requirements that I do not (at all) agree 
with like the specific requirement to use role based access control. 
What about NIST 800-162 (ABAC standard to supposedly replace RBAC at the 
fed level).

- Jim

@jmanico I do not really have a dog in this fight, but often work with customers in US government agencies and 800-53 is a requirement, not an optional choice for them when compiling authorization packages to allow their apps "to go to prod" after this authorization.

Where I do have a personal/focused professional interest in the mapping (where I do have a small personal interest): I need to build smaller, tactically-focused application security lists for development teams to do quick release reviews before that, and it is highly beneficial to indicate how actionable, application-focused items developers care about map to system objectives and organizational requirements that security officials (in the US government [FISMA system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FISMA#Security_controls) sense of the word) care about without repeat conversations or repeat work. That is almost always going to be, at a minimum some, most, or all of 800-53 contingent on how important the system is (impact level, to overly simplify). Hence I doubt my interest and that of other users who 👍ed is unique.

Maybe I am misunderstanding, but what does your or my disagreement on the applicability of the controls matter in the mapping? A lot of people do amend answers to certain controls or mark individual answers not applicable.

There is already an old Excel artifact in this repo, it is just no one has kept it up. Maybe there is value to mapping 800-162 as well. Is that what you are suggesting?

Let me rephrase my comment. I would certainly consider /some/ of 800-53 
controls for the next version of the ASVS standard.

- Jim
